# Jelly Bean Madness: Project Checklist

A pure-Java, no-CSS study site for the Unit 3 Data Structures test (searching, sorting, time complexity).

**Stack:** Java 21, built-in `com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer`, HTML generated by Java strings, no CSS, no JavaScript.

---

## 0. Setup

- [ ] Confirm `java -version` and `javac -version` both report 21
- [ ] Create `src/`, `out/` and `run.sh`
- [ ] Make `run.sh` compile into `out/` and start `Main`
- [ ] Add a `.gitignore` that excludes `out/`
- [ ] Write a "Hello, bean" `Main` and check `http://localhost:8080` loads

## 1. Web Foundation (`Main`, `Html`)

- [ ] Start `HttpServer` on port 8080 with a thread pool executor
- [ ] Write a routing table that maps a path to a handler
- [ ] Parse query strings (`?alg=bubble&step=3`)
- [ ] Parse POST form bodies (URL-decode them)
- [ ] Send responses with the correct `Content-Type` and UTF-8 charset
- [ ] Add a 404 page and a 500 page that shows no stack trace
- [ ] Write `Html.page(title, body)` so every page shares one layout
- [ ] Write the helpers `link`, `table`, `form`, `radio`, `pre` and `escape`
- [ ] Escape every user-supplied or code string, including Java snippets containing `<`
- [ ] Style only with HTML attributes (`bgcolor`, `<font color>`, `border`, `cellpadding`), with no CSS anywhere
- [ ] Build a shared nav bar with links to every mode

## 2. Sessions and Player Data

- [ ] Generate a random session ID and set it as a cookie
- [ ] Keep a `Map<String, Player>` of sessions
- [ ] `Player` holds the jar (bean counts by flavor), per-topic right/total, best scores and current game state
- [ ] Check behavior with no cookie, a bad cookie and a server restart
- [ ] Optional: save the jar to a file so it survives a restart

## 3. Core Java Model (the study material)

- [ ] `Bean implements Comparable<Bean>` with `compareTo` (by number)
- [ ] `Flavor` enum with a name and color
- [ ] Comparators: by flavor, by number descending, and by name length
- [ ] `Arrays.sort(beans, comparator)` demo page with a worked example
- [ ] `Frame` record: array snapshot, highlighted indices, message and comparison count
- [ ] `Algorithm` interface with `sort(int[])` and `frames(int[])`

## 4. Sorting and Searching (write from memory, then compare to the slides)

- [ ] Bubble sort with the early-exit `swapped` flag
- [ ] Selection sort
- [ ] Insertion sort
- [ ] Merge sort with the `temp` array
- [ ] Quick sort with `partition` and the last element as pivot
- [ ] Linear search that returns the index or -1
- [ ] Binary search, iterative
- [ ] Binary search, recursive
- [ ] A comparison counter in every algorithm
- [ ] A test `main` that checks every sort against `Arrays.sort` on random, sorted, reversed, duplicate and 0/1-element arrays
- [ ] A test that binary search finds every present value and returns -1 for absent ones
- [ ] Frame generators for all 5 sorts (merge sort records one frame per merge)

## 5. Question System

- [ ] Abstract `Question` class with prompt, optional code, options, answer index and explanation
- [ ] Subclasses or factories for each type (Big-O, detective, trace, table, concept)
- [ ] Shuffle the options and track the correct index after the shuffle
- [ ] `QuizSession` class with 10 questions, no repeats, score and streak
- [ ] A POST handler that checks the answer and shows the explanation
- [ ] A summary page at the end with beans earned and a replay link

## 6. Question Content (about 100 questions)

### Big-O code (about 20)

- [ ] O(1): arithmetic line, array index, loop bounded by a constant
- [ ] O(n): single loop, `i += 2`, two sequential loops
- [ ] O(log n): `i /= 2`, binary search, recursion that halves n
- [ ] O(n log n): `k *= 2` outer loop with an `n` inner loop
- [ ] O(n²): nested loops, an inner loop with `j < i`, selection sort
- [ ] O(n³), O(2ⁿ) (recursive fib) and O(n!) (conceptual)
- [ ] The rules: nested loops multiply, consecutive statements add and take the max, if/else takes the larger branch, drop constants

### Code detective (about 15)

- [ ] One question per algorithm, including both binary search versions
- [ ] The alternate insertion sort (`insertIndex` version)
- [ ] Fill-in-the-blank: `minIndex`, `key`, `n - i - 1`, `mid - 1`, `mid + 1`, `left == right`, `pivotIdx = high`

### Table (14 cards)

- [ ] Best and worst case for all 7 algorithms, using the guide's table
- [ ] Confirm the bubble sort best case with your teacher (the guide says O(n²), the slides say O(n)) and add a note
- [ ] Add a note on binary and linear search best cases (the guide's values vs strict O(1))

### Concepts (about 35)

- [ ] Linear vs binary search, and binary search needing a sorted list
- [ ] Divide and conquer (merge, quick) vs iterative in-place (bubble, insertion, selection)
- [ ] Match pseudocode lines to the algorithm they describe
- [ ] Quick sort worst case: the pivot is the min or max
- [ ] Merge sort extra memory, and why insertion sort is used inside quicksort
- [ ] Big-O vs Big-Omega vs Big-Theta, and why Big-O is not the same as worst case
- [ ] Time vs space complexity, and hardware being an external factor
- [ ] Doubling n: constant, log, linear, n log n and quadratic (use the corrected values)
- [ ] `compareTo`: positive, zero and negative results, and `"apple".compareTo("banana")`
- [ ] `Comparable` vs `Comparator`: when to use each
- [ ] Output of `Arrays.sort(strings, new StringLengthComparator())`
- [ ] What `maxElem` with a comparator returns

- [ ] **Bean Counter** (Big-O code quiz)
- [ ] **Code Detective** (algorithm recognition)
- [ ] **Table Time** (best/worst case cards)
- [ ] **Concept Candy** (theory and Java questions)

  - [ ] Run the algorithm to get the state after pass k
  - [ ] Create distractors from the previous pass, the next pass and a random swap, with no duplicate options
  - [ ] Add the quick sort first-partition and binary-search "which mids" variants
- [ ] **Sorter Lab** (visualizer)
  - [ ] Pick an algorithm and an input type (random, sorted, reversed)
  - [ ] Next and Prev links, with the step number in the URL
  - [ ] Autoplay using meta refresh
  - [ ] A comparison counter and a message for each step
  - [ ] Show the Java code and the pseudocode beside the frames

- [ ] **Binary Bean Hunt**
  - [ ] Hide values and show indices only
  - [ ] Higher/lower feedback, with eliminated beans greyed out
  - [ ] Score against ⌈log₂ n⌉ and give stars
  - [ ] Levels of 15, 31 and 63 beans
- [ ] **Complexity Ladder** (order the 7 classes)
- [ ] **Madness Mode** (mixed questions, 3 lives, streak bonus)
- [ ] **Recipe Book** (cheat sheet page with the tables, rules and code)

## 8. Jelly Bean Theme (no CSS)

- [ ] Pick a page `bgcolor` and a text color

- [ ] Add a jar page that shows the collection grouped by flavor
- [ ] Award a random flavor for each correct answer

- [ ] Walk through every mode start to finish

## 10. Study Tasks

- [ ] Write each sort from memory first, then compare with the slides
- [ ] Write the pseudocode for every algorithm in a comment above its method
- [ ] Recite the complexity table without looking
- [ ] Play Madness Mode until you hit 90% accuracy in every topic

## Reference: Complexity Table (from the review guide)

| Algorithm | Best Case | Worst Case |
|---|---|---|
| Selection Sort | O(n²) | O(n²) |
| Insertion Sort | O(n) | O(n²) |
| Bubble Sort | O(n²) | O(n²) |
| Merge Sort | O(n log n) | O(n log n) |
| Quick Sort | O(n log n) | O(n²) |
| Binary Search | O(log n) | O(log n) |
| Linear Search | O(n) | O(n) |

Growth order: O(1) < O(log n) < O(n) < O(n log n) < O(n²) < O(2ⁿ) < O(n!)

## Known Issues in the Course Materials

- **Bubble sort best case:** the guide says O(n²), the slides say O(n) because of the `swapped` early exit. Ask your teacher which the test uses.
- **Binary and linear search best case:** the guide lists O(log n) and O(n). Strictly, both are O(1) when the target is found on the first look.
- **Doubling table (the "Good Ones" slide):** the last column looks shifted. Correct values: O(log n) grows by one step, O(n) doubles, O(n log n) slightly more than doubles, O(n²) quadruples.
- **Bubble sort code (Sorting Algorithms slides):** `boolean swapped;` is never initialized, so it won't compile. It needs `= true`.
- **Merge sort code (same slides):** it redeclares `left` and `right` as arrays, so it won't compile. Delete those lines.
- **Quick sort code:** `high–-` contains a typo with a Unicode dash.
- **Quick sort pseudocode:** the partition uses `pIndex = beg - 1` and swaps at `pIndex` before incrementing, which is off by one.
- **Insertion sort best case slide:** it says "worst case for running time" but means best case.
